accepted.question_text: Does every connected harmonious graph admit a sequential labeling? A connected graph with e edges is harmonious when its vertices can be assigned distinct integers from 0 through e - 1 so that each edge xy receives the label f(x) + f(y) and the edge labels are distinct modulo e. A connected graph with e edges is sequential when its vertices can be assigned distinct integers from 0 through e - 1 so that the edge labels f(x) + f(y) form a block of e consecutive integers.

For positive integers m and n, determine whether the Cartesian-product grid graph C_{4m+2} x P_{2n+1} admits each of the following three labelings: an a-valuation, a graceful labeling, and a harmonious labeling. Here P_r is the path with r vertices, C_r is the cycle with r vertices, and G x H is the Cartesian product graph whose vertices are ordered pairs and whose edges join pairs that agree in one coordinate and are adjacent in the other. A graceful labeling of a connected graph with e edges assigns distinct vertex labels from 0 through e so that the absolute differences on edges are exactly 1 through e; an a-valuation is a graceful labeling with a threshold separating the endpoint labels of every edge; a harmonious labeling assigns distinct vertex labels from 0 through e - 1 so that edge sums are distinct modulo e.
accepted.context_brief: Labelings of C_{4m+2} x P_{2n+1} grids

accepted.question_text: For positive integers m and n with n > 2, does the Cartesian-product grid graph C_{2m+1} x P_n admit a graceful labeling? Here P_n is the path with n vertices, C_{2m+1} is the cycle with 2m + 1 vertices, and a graceful labeling of a connected graph with e edges assigns distinct vertex labels from 0 through e so that the absolute differences on edges are exactly 1 through e.

For positive integers m and n, in all cases not already covered by m = 1 and n > 1, does the Cartesian-product torus grid C_{4m} x C_{2n} admit a harmonious labeling? Here C_r is the cycle with r vertices, C_{4m} x C_{2n} is a Cartesian-product grid on a torus, and a harmonious labeling of a connected graph with e edges assigns distinct vertex labels from 0 through e - 1 so that edge sums are distinct modulo e.
